description: Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole is a culinary masterpiece, a rich and complex sauce deeply rooted in Oaxacan tradition. This iconic dish features a symphony of dried chiles, nuts, seeds, spices, and chocolate, simmered to perfection. Its distinctive dark color and profound flavor profile make it a truly unforgettable Mexican experience.

instructions.title: Prepare and Toast the Chiles
instructions.text: Heat a dry comal or skillet over medium heat. Toast the dried chiles for 30 seconds to 1 minute per side until fragrant, being careful not to burn them. Remove and immediately immerse in hot water for 20-30 minutes until softened. Drain and reserve the rehydrated chiles.

instructions.title: Roast Vegetables and Aromatics
instructions.text: In the same skillet, dry roast the tomatillos, tomatoes, onion, and garlic until softened and slightly charred, about 10-15 minutes. Set aside. In a separate pan with a little lard or oil, fry the plantain slices until golden brown. Set aside.

instructions.title: Toast Nuts, Seeds, and Spices
instructions.text: In a clean, dry skillet, toast the almonds, peanuts, pumpkin seeds, and sesame seeds separately until golden and fragrant. Be careful as sesame seeds toast quickly. Set aside. Lightly toast the cinnamon stick, cloves, peppercorns, anise seeds, oregano, and thyme for about 1 minute until aromatic. Set aside.

instructions.title: Blend the Mole Paste
instructions.text: Combine the rehydrated chiles, roasted vegetables, fried plantain, toasted nuts, seeds, and spices in a blender. Add 2 cups of chicken broth. Blend until very smooth, adding more broth as needed to achieve a thick, pourable consistency. This may require blending in batches. If desired, pass the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve for an even smoother sauce, pressing solids through.

instructions.title: Simmer the Mole Sauce
instructions.text: In a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat the remaining lard or oil over medium heat. Carefully pour in the blended mole paste. It will splatter, so be cautious. Cook, stirring constantly, for at least 20-30 minutes until the mole darkens significantly and thickens, reducing its volume. This step is crucial for developing the deep flavors.

instructions.title: Add Chocolate and Finish
instructions.text: Gradually stir in the remaining chicken broth, a cup at a time, bringing the mole to a gentle simmer. Add the chopped Mexican chocolate and stir until it is completely melted and incorporated. Season with salt to taste and add 1-2 teaspoons of sugar if needed to balance the flavors. Continue to simmer for at least 30 minutes, or up to an hour, stirring occasionally, until the mole reaches your desired consistency and the flavors have fully melded.

instructions.title: Serve Your Mole Negro
instructions.text: Add your cooked chicken or turkey pieces directly into the mole sauce to heat through, or serve the mole generously over individual portions of meat. Garnish with a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. Serve hot with warm corn tortillas and Mexican rice.

tips: To achieve a truly authentic flavor, ensure you properly toast each ingredient without burning. Burnt ingredients will make the mole bitter.
For an extra layer of flavor, use high-quality Mexican chocolate (like Ibarra or Mayordomo) and fresh, dried chiles. Do not skip the straining step for the smoothest mole.
Mole Negro improves with age. Make it a day or two in advance and refrigerate; the flavors will deepen. Reheat gently, adding a little more broth if it has thickened too much.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of Oaxaca, Mexico, where a dish of unparalleled depth and complexity reigns supreme: Mole Negro. More than just a sauce, Mole Negro is a cultural icon, a testament to generations of culinary wisdom, and a celebration of indigenous ingredients. For those seeking truly authentic Mexican dinner recipes, mastering Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole is an incredibly rewarding endeavor, transforming your kitchen into a vibrant testament to Mexican heritage.

## What is Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole?

Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole stands as the most revered and intricate of Oaxaca's seven moles. It is a masterpiece of balance, characterized by its deep, almost black color and a flavor profile that is simultaneously sweet, savory, smoky, and subtly spicy. This isn't a quick sauce; it's a labor of love, traditionally reserved for major celebrations like weddings, baptisms, and Day of the Dead. Its darkness comes from a meticulous process of roasting and charring a multitude of ingredients, particularly a specific blend of dried chilies. Unlike other moles, Mole Negro often incorporates plantains, raisins, and a significant amount of Mexican chocolate, which contributes to its rich color and complex finish, rather than making it taste overtly sweet. The sheer number of components—often exceeding 20 or even 30—each carefully prepared, toasted, fried, or ground, is what gives this mole its legendary status and profound depth of flavor.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting authentic Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole requires a diverse array of ingredients, many of which are essential for its distinctive flavor. While specific quantities vary by recipe and household, here’s a general breakdown of what you'll typically need:

*   **Dried Chilies**: The backbone of the mole. A mix of chilhuacle negro (if available, crucial for color and flavor), mulato, pasilla mexicano, and ancho chilies. These are usually toasted and rehydrated.
*   **Nuts and Seeds**: Almonds, peanuts, pecans, sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds. These contribute to the mole’s texture and richness.
*   **Spices**: Cinnamon stick, whole cloves, black peppercorns, cumin seeds, star anise, oregano, thyme.
*   **Aromatics**: White onion, garlic, tomatoes, tomatillos.
*   **Sweet and Fruity Elements**: Plantain, raisins, prunes, Mexican chocolate (essential for depth and color, not just sweetness).
*   **Thickeners and Enhancers**: Tortillas or stale bread, often a small amount of sugar or piloncillo.
*   **Fats and Liquids**: Lard or vegetable oil for frying, rich chicken or turkey broth.
*   **Seasoning**: Salt to taste.

Sourcing high-quality ingredients, especially the chilies, will make a significant difference in the final taste of your Mole Negro.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

While a full recipe would include precise measurements, here's a general guide to the intricate process of making Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole:

1.  **Prepare the Chilies**: Carefully toast the dried chilies on a comal or dry skillet until fragrant, being careful not to burn them. Remove stems and seeds, then rehydrate them in hot water until softened.
2.  **Toast Nuts, Seeds, and Spices**: In separate batches, toast the various nuts and seeds until golden. Do the same for the whole spices, releasing their aromatic oils.
3.  **Fry Aromatics and Fruits**: Fry chopped onions, garlic, tomatoes, tomatillos, and the plantain, raisins, and prunes until softened and slightly caramelized.
4.  **Make the Paste**: Combine the rehydrated chilies, toasted nuts, seeds, spices, fried aromatics, fruits, and torn tortillas/bread in a blender with some broth. Blend in batches until you achieve a very smooth paste. This may require multiple blending cycles and straining.
5.  **Fry the Mole Paste**: This is a crucial step. In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat lard or oil. Add the mole paste and fry it over medium heat, stirring constantly, for at least 30-45 minutes. This process deepens the flavor, cooks out any raw taste, and prevents the mole from separating. The paste will darken further and become incredibly fragrant.
6.  **Simmer with Broth**: Gradually add warm chicken or turkey broth to the fried paste, stirring constantly to incorporate. Bring to a gentle simmer.
7.  **Add Chocolate and Season**: Stir in the Mexican chocolate until fully melted and incorporated. Continue to simmer the mole for at least 1-2 hours, or even longer, allowing the flavors to meld and deepen. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt, and a touch of sugar if needed to balance the flavors. The mole should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Making Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole is an art form, and these tips can help you achieve a truly exceptional result:

*   **Don't Rush the Roasting/Toasting**: Each ingredient needs to be perfectly toasted—not burnt—to unlock its full flavor potential. This step contributes significantly to the mole's complexity.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth**: A smooth mole is a sign of a well-made one. If your blender isn't powerful enough, strain the blended paste through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any fibrous bits from the chilies or nuts.
*   **Embrace the "Frying" of the Paste**: This isn't just a quick sauté. Frying the mole paste thoroughly for an extended period transforms its flavor and texture. It’s essential for that signature rich, deep taste.
*   **Quality Mexican Chocolate**: Use authentic Mexican chocolate, which often contains cinnamon and other spices, rather than regular unsweetened cocoa powder. It adds a unique depth that cannot be replicated.
*   **Patience is a Virtue**: Mole Negro is a slow-cooked dish. The long simmering time allows all the myriad flavors to integrate and develop. The longer it simmers (within reason), the better it tastes.
*   **Make Ahead**: Mole Negro often tastes even better the next day, after the flavors have had more time to meld. It also freezes beautifully.

## Serving Suggestions

Once your exquisite Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole is ready, the possibilities for serving are delicious and varied.

*   **Traditional with Poultry**: The most classic pairing is with roasted or poached turkey (pavo en mole) or chicken. Drizzle generously over pieces of poultry, ensuring every bite is coated in the rich sauce.
*   **Rice and Tortillas**: Always serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping up the luscious sauce, and a side of fluffy white rice to soak up any extra.
*   **Enchiladas**: Transform leftover chicken or fresh cheese into incredible enchiladas by generously coating them with the mole.
*   **Tamales**: Use the mole as a filling for tamales, or pour it over plain tamales for an extra layer of flavor.
*   **Vegetarian Options**: Mole Negro can also complement vegetarian dishes beautifully. Try it over roasted sweet potatoes, grilled plantains, or even hearty mushrooms like portobellos. It also pairs wonderfully with refried beans.
*   **Breakfast**: Believe it or not, some regions enjoy mole over scrambled eggs for a hearty and flavorful breakfast.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the traditional Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole is a specific and revered recipe, there are always ways to adapt it based on ingredient availability or personal preference.

*   **Chilies**: If chilhuacle negro chilies are impossible to find, you can still make a delicious mole using a combination of mulato, ancho, and pasilla chilies, though the color and specific flavor profile will be slightly different. Some recipes might include a very small amount of morita or chipotle for an extra smoky kick.
*   **Nuts and Seeds**: Feel free to adjust the ratio of nuts and seeds based on what you have, ensuring you maintain a good balance for texture and flavor.
*   **Sweeteners**: While Mexican chocolate provides most of the sweetness, a touch of piloncillo (Mexican brown sugar cone) or dark brown sugar can be used to round out the flavors if needed.
*   **Protein**: While turkey and chicken are traditional, mole can also be served with pork loin, duck, or even firm white fish.
*   **Spice Level**: For those who prefer less heat, remove more seeds and veins from the chilies before rehydrating. For more heat, leave some in or add a tiny amount of a hotter chili like arbol.

Making Mole Negro Oaxacan Black Mole is a culinary adventure that connects you to centuries of Mexican tradition. It demands time and dedication, but the reward is an unparalleled depth of flavor that truly embodies the soul of Oaxaca. This complex, aromatic, and deeply satisfying sauce is more than just a meal; it's an experience, a celebration, and a testament to the rich tapestry of Mexican dinner recipes.
